verdict.rationale: Ente's own self-hosting documentation describes running Ente Auth against your own machine (http://<machine-ip>:3003). Ente states its server is open source, and Auth sync is end-to-end encrypted. This shows a first-party self-hosted sync path, but the evidence is a single thin line with no detail on server deployment or perimeter controls. Missing for 10: detailed server deployment docs, confirmation that all sync and secrets stay on self-hosted infrastructure, independent or hands-on self-hosting reports.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the sync server on my own infrastructure and keep every secret inside my perimeter

citations.quote: Alternatively, if using Ente Auth, get started by adding an account (assuming you are running Ente Auth at `http://<machine-ip>:3003` or `http://localhost:3003`).
Ente's apps and server are open source
Your codes sync across all your devices, end-to-end encrypted.
